retro:
# Retrospective: PR 12778

## What worked

Fresh Fable High and Astra Xhigh sessions independently reached the makepkg configuration boundary. Separate private fixtures prevented runtime sharing and both reports were saved before synthesis. Real makepkg plus tiny Make/CMake/Ninja tasks distinguished entry-point environment success from actual backend behavior without heavy compilation or installation. Baseline controls established incomplete new control rather than a new regression. Coordinator raw-output inspection and seal verification complemented the reviewer assessments.

## Friction and process improvements

Environment-only tests at yay would miss the important behavior; future similar work should keep a lightweight real configuration/backend boundary. The Fable report pursued more scheduler detail than warranted in the public comment, but those autonomous observations remain useful local limitations. Adjudication prioritized an actual explicit-override failure rather than forcing consensus on severity or including every possible advisory change.

Some documentation endpoints were unavailable or guessed incorrectly; reviewers retained documented limits and used available official source. No confirmed review.py or Omadev defect occurred. No desktop reservation was necessary and no Omadev feature request follows from this review.

## Cleanup and carry-forward

All five isolated runs are sealed and retained. Private runtimes were torn down; sources remain clean. No host configuration, service, package, hardware, account, audio, firewall or browser-profile mutation occurred. Reviewer panes and session history remain available. The coordinator did not restart itself, post, or open HTML. Each final-draft editorial check uses its own new Medium session. Publication and next assignment remain solely with the outer assistant.
comment:
The advertised Make job cap can be replaced by makepkg configuration.

**Verified:** starting from niceness 0, the updated invocation and its tested build children run at niceness 15 and best-effort I/O priority 7. Job defaults, the one-job floor, explicit overrides, yay arguments, and skip paths behaved as intended at the yay boundary.

### makepkg configuration can override the selected Make job count

At [`omarchy-update-aur-pkgs:17-21`](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/blob/47a2cc14e65e0a8bf68bb1f7eab701d3f2d0502c/bin/omarchy-update-aur-pkgs#L17-L21), `MAKEFLAGS` is supplied only through the environment. Real makepkg 7.1.0 subsequently sources its configuration, which can replace that value:

```text
Synthetic config: MAKEFLAGS="-j4"
OMARCHY_AUR_BUILD_JOBS=1
  updater passes MAKEFLAGS=-j1
    makepkg loads config: MAKEFLAGS=-j4
      Make runs 4 concurrent test jobs, not 1
```

**Impact:** users with a configured Make job count do not receive the selected per-update cap, even with an explicit one-job override. Lower priority still applies. This is incomplete parallelism control, not newly introduced oversubscription or a reproduced desktop freeze. With no configured `MAKEFLAGS`, the new value survives.

**Suggested change:** apply the selected Make job count after makepkg configuration is loaded, preserving unrelated Make flags, or explicitly document that makepkg configuration takes precedence over this override. A replacement implementation was not tested.

**Scope correction:** describe these as job-count defaults for cooperating tools, not a guarantee that foreground work retains half the CPU. With all three environment values set for two jobs, the same four-task synthetic workload reached two concurrent jobs through `cmake --build`, but four through direct Ninja. The priority settings still applied in both cases.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** head `47a2cc14e65e0a8bf68bb1f7eab701d3f2d0502c` against merge-base `8f324c90b82790d31ab33565441e07cbdb8d2308`. Production updater, mocked package/network gates and yay orchestration, real makepkg/Make/CMake/Ninja, and small synthetic jobs. No real AUR compilation or installation, Cargo build, desktop-responsiveness benchmark, or disk-scheduler performance test. Setting priorities does not establish their effect across CPU task groups or storage schedulers.

**Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Automated AI review:** Astra initial inspection, independent Fable 5.1 and separate Astra reviews, followed by coordinator verification of claims against source and targeted saved evidence.
